elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.9 requires USD 5,000,000 of cyber liability insurance only where HDI processes “Confidential Information or user information of the Company.” It does not use or establish equivalence to the required “Customer Data” trigger, and processing of Customer Data is not demonstrably absent. The non-operative margin comment cannot cure that mismatch.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Although the stated cyber limit is USD 5,000,000, the obligation is triggered by processing “Confidential Information or user information of the Company,” not by processing Customer Data. No operative language establishes that these triggers are coextensive, and Customer Data processing is not demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The clause meets the CGL, E&O, workers' compensation, and certificate requirements, and its cyber limit exceeds both positions. However, the cyber obligation uses a materially different trigger from processing Customer Data, so neither complete level is satisfied. The edit is also not minimal because it imposes an additional one-year post-termination maintenance period for all listed coverage, which neither position requires. The existing headings and counterparts provision remains effective, and no direct contradiction is introduced.
